newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Tuesday, Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Tuesday, Dec 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- PETROLEUM EXCHANGE RULES OUT MERGER WITH LIFFE

The London-based International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) has rejected speculation it may merge with the London International Financial Futures Exchange (Liffe). The merger suggestion was mooted following recent comments from the chairman of Liffe that IPE was a potential takeover target. The IPE has said it intends to remain independent and to develop into the leading centre of energy trading in Europe.
-- CABLE GROUPS CONSIDER LEGAL CHALLENGE TO BSKYB PRICES

The Cable Communications Association, which represents UK cable operators, has responded angrily to news the Office of Fair Trading has approved a new industry pricing structure. The CCA is considering a judicial review of the decision, which endorses a new rate card from satellite broadcaster BSkyB. The rate card determines the price BSkyB charges the cable operators for carrying its television channels.
-- FISCHLER PRESSES FOR EU FOOD WATCHDOG

The European Union agriculture commissioner, Franz Fischler, has unveiled controversial proposals for an independent consumer watchdog on food safety. The measures are likely to be opposed by member states keen to keep their own sovereignty over food safety issues and their potential political implications.
-- INVESTMENT GROUP OFFERS FUND DEALING OVER INTERNET

The UK investment banking and fund management group Flemings is to offer a service enabling retail customers to deal in its funds via the Internet. The move heralds a new milestone in the use of the Internet by the financial services industry, which also offers electronic discount retail stockbroking.
-- DRUGS COMPANIES DIAGNOSE AN ACUTE BRAIN DEFICIENCY

According to a Financial Times report, some executives in Britain's largest pharmaceutical companies fear the declining quality of graduates in the UK could mean the industry in Britain is unable to sustain its world-beating status into the next century. The companies, including SmithKline Beecham, Glaxo Wellcome and Zeneca, blame the government for not investing in the scientific infrastructure.
-- MPS CRITICISE OFT CHIEF ON PETROL RETAILING

The Commons trade and industry committee has heard an assurance from John Bridgeman, director-general of fair trading, that his office will take steps to protect independent petrol retailers in the increasingly bitter battle with the large petrol companies. The independents claim they are being squeezed out of business by the larger companies, in particular by the petrol price war initiated last year by Esso.
-- BASS SELLS 61 US HOLIDAY INNS

UK-based brewer and hotels group Bass is to dispose of almost all its Holiday Inns in North America. Bass will receive $391 million cash from Dallas-based outfit Bristol Hotel Company for 61 owned and managed Holiday Inn hotels. Bass is also to receive a 36 percent stake in Bristol, taking the total value of the cash and equity deal to $640 million.
-- MGAM TO PAY OUT 200 MILLION STG OVER UNIT TRUST LOSSES

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management the fund management company hit by an investment scandal involving unit trust manager Peter Young, is to pay about 200 million stg in compensation to some 90,000 investors affected by the affair. Young was sacked following the discovery he invested funds in unlisted holding companies in Luxembourg. Although the Serious Fraud Office is investigating the matter, Young has yet to be charged.
-- LLOYDS CHEMISTS PUTS PRESSURE ON RIVAL SUITORS

UK-based pharmacy group Lloyds Chemists has urged its shareholders to hold out for a higher offer in the high-profile bidding war between suitors Gehe and UniChem. The German company Gehe has offered 500p a share in cash while UniChem's predominantly share offer values Lloyds at 483.8p a share. Both bidders have until January 17 to increase their offers.
-- CALENERGY HITS OUT AT NORTHERN'S VALUATION

Independent U.S. power producer CalEnergy has hit back at claims by its UK-based takeover target Northern Electricity over the 782 million stg hostile bid. CalEnergy alleged Northern had made 'misleading and incorrect' statements regarding the value of the bid, in particular that it was mean by comparision with other bids in the sector.
